punchline: Fisher and Ury say to yield to principle, not pressure; the simplest case is one person cuts and the other picks first.
thirty_sec: In Getting to Yes, Fisher and Ury insist on objective criteria. The simplest case is dividing a dessert: one cuts, the other chooses, so the cutter cuts evenly. At the Law of the Sea Conference, the United States and India disagreed over a mining fee. Both looked at an economic model developed at MIT, and both reconsidered. A quick test the authors suggest: would the other side accept these terms if the roles were reversed?
